disclaimer: Document attestation, PRO, translation, and Chamber fees vary by document and route. Verify the current service quote. The UAE is not listed in the HCCH Apostille Convention status table checked on 5 September 2026; foreign-document requirements must be confirmed with the relevant UAE mission and receiving authority.

attestation.apostille_correction_note: The UAE is absent from the official HCCH Apostille Convention status table checked on 5 September 2026. An apostille alone must not be assumed to replace applicable UAE attestation requirements.

legalization_chain.name: Home country Ministry of Foreign Affairs (or State Department)
UAE Embassy in the home country
UAE MOFAIC in Dubai or Abu Dhabi
Translation into Arabic by an MOJ-registered legal translator if the receiving authority requires certified Arabic translation

fees.scope_note: Legacy document-class fees retained from the earlier review. The current service page routes by document and destination; confirm the application quote and any mission or courier charge.

documents_typically_attested: Foreign criminal record / good conduct certificate
attestation.legalization_chain_note: Illustrative foreign-document sequence. Notarisation, prior authentication, embassy steps and Arabic translation depend on the document, issuing country, electronic mission service and receiving authority; not every case requires five physical steps.

digital_attestation.scope: Eligible original digital documents issued in the UAE for use outside the UAE.
digital_attestation.route_selection: The MoFA application selects digital or approved-courier processing based on issuing authority and document type.
digital_attestation.input_note: Use the original verifiable digital PDF; a scan or photograph is not an original digital document.
digital_attestation.foreign_documents: Use the UAE Missions Abroad service and check the mission website for electronic availability or in-person requirements.

what_a_pro_does: Visa processing (entry permit, status change, stamping)
pro_services.when_you_need_one: Mainland licenses with 3+ visas typically have an in-house PRO. Smaller setups outsource to PRO firms.
pro_services.pricing_basis: Private-provider market estimate only. The ranges are not a government tariff, exclude government and third-party transaction fees, and vary by scope and provider. Obtain an itemised quote before budgeting.
pro_services.pro_vs_setup_consultant_vs_csp: PRO handles operational paperwork after incorporation. Setup consultant handles incorporation itself. Corporate services provider does both plus accounting and compliance.

mandatory_for: Court filings or instruments when the receiving court requires an Arabic legal translation
Government submissions when the receiving authority requires a certified Arabic translation
Foreign-language records used in a regulated transaction when the receiving authority specifies legal translation
legal_translation.approved_translators_scope: Where legal translation is required, use a legal translator registered with the Ministry of Justice and confirm the receiving authority's current document rules.
legal_translation.registry: Ministry of Justice registered legal translators
legal_translation.pricing_basis: Private-provider market estimate only. MOJ does not publish the AED 50 to 150 per-page range or the urgency uplift as an official tariff. Obtain a quote and confirm whether the receiving authority requires legal translation.

chamber_of_commerce.name: Dubai Chamber of Commerce
chamber_of_commerce.mandatory_for: DET licensees conducting listed commercial, industrial, agricultural, professional, or service activities, subject to statutory exemptions
chamber_of_commerce.statutory_exemptions: The governing law permits exemptions for specified micro and small enterprises and manual professions and trades, as set by the Chamber's board resolution.
chamber_of_commerce.free_zone_membership: A free zone establishment may join after approval of its supervising free zone authority.
chamber_of_commerce.fee_exemption: Eligible Mohammed Bin Rashid Establishment for SME Development members are exempt for five years.
chamber_of_commerce.fee_notes: The official renewal schedule varies by legal form, owner nationality, and activity. Use the applicable category rather than treating AED 50 or AED 2,200 as a universal fee.

certificate_of_origin.purpose: Certifies the origin of goods for export or re-export

common_mistakes.title: Choosing the wrong activity code
common_mistakes.impact: Limits banking, invoicing, and hiring downstream. Cannot be changed without a full license amendment.
common_mistakes.fix: Look up DET activity list on app.invest.dubai.ae before applying. If unsure, choose a broader activity that covers your intended business.

common_mistakes.title: Picking the cheapest free zone without checking bank acceptance
common_mistakes.impact: Bank onboarding depends on the bank, account product, activity and applicant documentation; a low licence price does not determine account acceptance.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the current account criteria and onboarding assistance before choosing a jurisdiction.

common_mistakes.title: Assuming a free zone licence automatically covers onshore activity
common_mistakes.impact: Invoicing a mainland customer is not by itself the legal test. A Dubai free zone establishment that conducts activity outside its free zone must use the applicable DET licence or permit route, and eligibility depends on the activity and required authority approvals.
common_mistakes.fix: Compare a mainland DET licence with the branch-licence or temporary-permit route under Dubai Executive Council Resolution 11 of 2025. Confirm the activity on DET's current eligibility list before trading onshore.

common_mistakes.title: Underestimating the AED 5,000 to 15,000 in PRO and translation fees
common_mistakes.impact: These costs are not in the headline license price and often surprise first-time founders.
common_mistakes.fix: Budget AED 5,000 to 15,000 on top of the license cost for PRO services, MOFA attestation, and legal translation.

common_mistakes.title: Not budgeting for the 1 to 16 week bank account delay
common_mistakes.impact: Founders cannot operate, pay employees, or process payments without a bank account.
common_mistakes.fix: Apply to 2 or 3 banks in parallel. Consider Wio for fast onboarding while traditional banks process.

common_mistakes.title: Not getting Ejari before applying for visa quota
common_mistakes.impact: Ejari is a precondition for visa quota in mainland setups. Delays the entire visa pipeline.
common_mistakes.fix: Sign and register Ejari first, then start the visa application chain.

common_mistakes.title: Choosing a high-risk industry without preparation
common_mistakes.impact: Crypto, forex, jewelry, used cars, money service businesses face heavy KYC and frequent rejection.
common_mistakes.fix: Prepare extensive source-of-funds documentation, choose a free zone aligned with your industry, and consider VARA licensing for crypto.

common_mistakes.title: Letting the license lapse
common_mistakes.impact: Late-renewal penalties and reactivation requirements vary by licensing authority and licence status; the earlier universal AED 5,000 plus AED 250/month figure was not supported.
common_mistakes.fix: Set a calendar reminder 60 days before renewal.

common_mistakes.title: Trying to operate without UAE Pass in 2025/2026
common_mistakes.impact: UAE Pass is required for almost every government e-service. Operating without it forces you to use slow physical channels.
common_mistakes.fix: Register for UAE Pass on day one. Verify to the highest level (full verification with Emirates ID + biometrics).

common_mistakes.title: Mixing up the three Dubai Chambers
common_mistakes.impact: Joining the wrong chamber wastes the membership fee and provides irrelevant services.
common_mistakes.fix: Mainland commercial license holders join Dubai Chamber of Commerce by default. International trade focus joins Dubai International Chamber. Tech/digital startups engage with DCDE through programs (no standalone membership).
